Subject: BrightCart trial onboarding: traffic intake & acceptance checklist

Hi Alyssa —

Great call earlier today, thanks for walking us through BrightCart's checkout flow. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the post-call recap, proposed POC scope, and the specific traffic/profile data we need to finalize the trial environment. This will help Karthik size the Dedicated trial and set the success criteria.

Quick recap (TL;DR):
- Objective: 2-week POC to validate correctness and cost/latency for the checkout assistant (search suggestions + confirmation copy).
- Success criteria (draft): functional parity on top-10 intents, 95th pctl generation latency under 350ms for 75% of traffic, no production-facing errors during peak bursts, and token-cost per session within budget target.
- Next steps: BrightCart sends canonical sample payloads + hourly RPS/peak windows; Redwood provides trial config, monitoring dashboard and kickoff date.

Traffic/profile items we need from you (see attached sample csv):
1) Average sustained RPS during business hours (Mon-Fri, 09:00-18:00 local)
2) Peak burst RPS and typical burst duration (e.g., 120 RPS for ~45s)
3) Typical concurrency (number of simultaneous sessions hitting generation concurrently)
4) Average prompt tokens and average completion tokens (or token distribution bins: 0-50, 51-200, 201-500)
5) Percent of requests that are short (<= 64 tokens) vs long (> 256 tokens)
6) Retry patterns / client-side backoff behavior
7) Any geo/regulatory constraints (PII-sensitive flows)

Draft timeline (subject to your data):
- 2026-06-29: Kickoff + infra handoff (trial environment created)
- 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-13: Trial execution and daily checks
- 2026-07-14: Review + acceptance decision

Ownership suggestions:
- BrightCart: provide payload samples, traffic.csv (see template), infra contact for VPN/whitelisted IPs, and acceptance signoff.
- Redwood: provision Dedicated trial, baseline run, monitoring dashboards, and daily standup (15m).

I've attached a draft trial acceptance checklist (redwood_trial_checklist.xlsx) and a sample traffic template (brightcart_traffic_profile.csv) — fill those in and we'll finalize the kickoff.

If any of the items above need to change, call it out and we'll adapt. Proposed kickoff time: Tue 2026-06-29 10:00 PT. Does that work for you?

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear recap and the templates. I attached our initial traffic extract (brightcart_traffic_profile.csv) — it's an anonymized sample of one week. High-level numbers below:

- Average sustained RPS (business hours): 9–14 RPS
- Typical concurrency across checkout services: ~18 concurrent generation requests
- Peak bursts: we see spikes up to 85 RPS, typically lasting 20–60s around promo pushes (we have a weekly email campaign on Wed afternoons)
- Token profile: median prompt tokens = 95, median completion tokens = 210; 60% of requests fall in 64–256 token combined length, ~10% are >500 tokens (order summarization flows)
- Retry/backoff: client retries with exponential backoff, max 2 retries after 500ms then drop

Thanks for the dataset, Alyssa — useful detail. A few clarifying Qs and recommended test matrix from the SE side: 

Clarifications:
- When you say "concurrency ~18", is that sustained during peak windows or an average across endpoints? We need the peak concurrent generator counts per endpoint to size KV cache and batchers.
- For the ~10% >500 tokens flows: are those synchronous calls that must meet the same latency SLOs, or can we classify them as background (accept higher latency)?

Redwood trial test recommendations (proposed):
1) Baseline correctness run at 0.5x observed peak (approx 40 RPS) to validate output quality and integration.
2) Sustained load run at 1x observed peak (85 RPS) for 10 minutes to validate stability.
3) Burst stress tests: ramp to 120–150 RPS for 30–60s to observe fallback behavior and error rates.
4) Long-tail token test: run 200 sequential summarization requests (>=500 tokens) to measure cost and latency distribution.

Suggested acceptance criteria (we can finalize with you):
- Functional: top-10 intent pass rate >= 95% on validated test prompts.
- Latency: p95 generation <= 350ms for foreground flows; p95 for background summarization <= 2s.
- Errors: end-to-end failures (HTTP 5xx or empty responses) < 0.5% during sustained runs.

Operational notes: we'll enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, continuous batching (with tight tail latency profile), and a fallback model variant for peak collapse. For the trial we'll expose the Redwood Console dashboard and token-level cost breakdown.

I'll prepare a trial config doc and pre-populate the redwood_trial_checklist.xlsx with recommended settings.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

- Cost: average tokens/session within the projected budget we discussed in the call (I will add exact $/token numbers after the baseline).
